tests: Automated validation: 16 xUnit tests passed and 0 failed. They cover heat-map aggregation, real SQLite save, reopen, and clear behavior, invalid coordinates, permission denial, storage failure, duplicate starts, and cancellation of pending GPS requests.
builds: Solution restore succeeded. The Android Debug build (net10.0-android) and the iOS simulator build (net10.0-ios, iossimulator-arm64) both succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Xcode 27.1 is newer than the Xcode 26.6 required by the installed .NET for iOS 26.5 workload, so the iOS build used -p:ValidateXcodeVersion=false; Microsoft documents such version combinations as unsupported even when they build and run.
runtime: The app was run on an iOS 27.1 simulator (Xcode 27.1) with Apple Maps, using simulated GPS positions near Williamsburg, Kentucky. Every reading came through the app's normal location service and was saved in SQLite; no records were inserted directly. The location permission prompt appeared with the app's purpose text and was allowed while in use. Tracking saved a reading about every eight seconds: 124 samples across 12 positions. Stop Tracking held, with no new rows for 20 seconds. After a force-stop and relaunch, the app showed 'Ready — saved history restored', the same 76 samples and circles, and did not restart tracking. Longer dwell times produced visibly different blue, amber, and red cells (largest cells: 45, 28, and 17 samples). Opening Settings stopped tracking; the count stayed at 124 for 24 seconds in the background and 24 seconds after returning, with tracking not resumed. After the map was panned away, Center on Current Location moved it back to the latest recorded position. On the Android emulator (API 36), the app installed, launched, showed the permission prompt, saved emulator GPS readings, and restored them after relaunch; Clear History showed a confirmation, Cancel kept the history, Delete removed all records and overlays, and a relaunch showed zero samples. Android map tiles were not shown because no Google Maps key was configured; permission denial is covered by an automated test rather than a live run.
